gaps.requirement: UI accuracy and 'Exactly what do I click or type': steps use the real labels of the current software (section 6, priority 2). The form-driven steps of Track B are the critical path.
gaps.current: The three guides that drive the Streamlit form do not match it. (a) initialise_repository.md:12 says to select 'Start initialisation' 'in the **Initialise a repository** section'. The form's subheader is 'Initialise GitHub repository' (app.py:838). The guide's example version is '0.1.0' (line 6) but the form recommends 0.0.1 (app.py:869). The guide never names 'Validate submission', 'GitHub repository URL', 'Personal Access Token' or 'Create pull request', and says only 'Follow the instructions on the website', although the form cannot finish without a token (app.py:960-977). (b) notebook_upload.md:143 says 'Click **Validate submission**' in the update flow. The button there is 'Validate & Add Submission' (app.py:1029), followed by a Submission list step the guide omits. (c) The form accepts only a classic token starting 'ghp_' and rejects fine-grained 'github_pat_' tokens (app.py:972-977, 1137-1139). template_synchronization.md tells readers to create a fine-grained token. personal_access_token.md describes a hybrid: classic path but uses 'Name' (l.17,36), 'Resource owner' (l.35) and 'repo > contents' (l.20,39), and offers 'Read-Only Access' (l.29). GitHub's own page (docs.github.com, fetched today) says the classic field is 'Note', there is no Resource owner for classic tokens, and the scope is plain 'repo'. The same page says organisations may block classic tokens with a 403, which the guide never mentions. (d) installer_images.md:9-11 calls the images Logo/Banner/Header; the form calls them 'Project icon image', 'Project welcome image', 'Project headers image' (app.py:894-908).

gaps.requirement: Release changes trigger review of the relevant docs; 'preview per relevant pull request, validate links, run basic docs tests before publishing' (section 6, section 7 Maintenance, priority 5).
gaps.current: In the site repo, publish.yml runs on pull_request, but it builds against the template's default branch (checkout of CellMigrationLab/LabConstrictor and doc_source with no ref) and fetch_guides.py without --ref, so a PR to the template or a plugin repo is never rendered. The 'preview' is a zipped artifact (upload-artifact 'site-preview', 14 days) that someone must download and serve, not a link. Doc changes in other repos appear only on the next push to the site or the 05:23 UTC cron, and a break then shows as a failed daily run plus an issue. NucleiSky has an ISSUE_TEMPLATE/documentation.yml, the template does not. fetch_guides.py already supports --ref for exactly this preview.

gaps.requirement: Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA, keyboard, accessible images, no unnecessary large animations, appropriately sized screenshots on mobile) and Google image guidance (cropped screenshots, efficient alternatives to GIF).
gaps.current: Five guides embed GIFs that autoplay and loop forever (GIF loop=0): Accept_PR.gif 36 s 5.2 MB, GitHub_Access_Token.gif 15 s 3.2 MB, Synchronisation_Secret_Creation.gif 60 s 1.4 MB, Synchronisation_Token_Creation.gif 66 s 3.3 MB, Upload_src.gif 27 s 4.5 MB (about 17.7 MB in total, each 1280x720 shown at 328x185 px on a phone). They have no pause control, so they fail WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide) and the mobile-weight rule. Alt text describes the medium, not the content: 'Gif of generating a GitHub token', 'Upload external code GIF', 'GIF showing the token creation'; no guide image sits in a figure with a caption, and DESIGN.md/check_design.py enforce only that alt exists (check_design.py:159-165). Several screenshots are wide strips that become unreadable on a phone: PR_tab.png 1908x271 renders 47 px high at 375 px, Download_Notebook.png 1910x308 renders 53 px high, Use_Template.png 1903x537 renders 93 px high; Customisation_Default.png is 2961x2239, 1.3 MB. Images have no width/height attributes. I ran axe-core 4.10.2 (wcag2a/aa, 21aa, 22aa, best-practice) at 1280 and 375 px on 13 pages: every page shows aria-required-attr on the search input (role=combobox without aria-expanded/aria-controls), two buttons with no accessible name (theme search widget), link-in-text-block for the footer 'Cell Migration Lab' link (colour only, 1.82:1 against surrounding text), and on /apps/, /build/ and the home page 'small' tag labels at 3.34:1 (needs 4.5:1). Nothing in CI runs an accessibility test.
